name: Man at Bar Recognizes Pacifico on Television
description: A man sitting at the bar turns his head sharply toward the television when he hears the name Pacifico during a broadcast of a game. His attention intensifies, recalling a previous moment when he saw Lou kick a ball that struck the godfather's hat and knocked it off.

name: Linebacker Delivers Hard Tackle to Running Back's Throat
description: Under a bright fall sky at The Big O stadium, a Miami Dolphins linebacker lunges at a Washington Redskins running back during a regular-season NFL game. As the two collide, the linebacker drives his elbow into the runner's throat, bringing him down hard on the turf. The crowd of seventy-six thousand fans reacts instantly, the air thick with noise and tension, as the game pauses momentarily around the fallen player.

name: Jamal and Shane Find Sabotaged Trip Wire as Team Emerges
description: Jamal and Shane crouch near the trip wire, inspecting it closely. Their expressions tighten as they realize it has been tampered with. At that moment, an announcement crackles over the loudspeaker: 'And now... uh, the rest of the Washington Redskins.' The remaining players shuffle out of the tunnel and onto the field without fanfare, walking past the two men still kneeling by the damaged wire.

description: McGinty approaches Sid with Shane, who is wearing a heavily reinforced helmet with an intricate face guard that obscures his vision. McGinty points at the helmet and questions how Shane can see well enough to play quarterback. Sid explains that Shane told him he was a linebacker. Shane insists he can see. McGinty holds up three fingers, and Shane hesitates before incorrectly guessing the number.

description: A nondescript van pulls up. Earl Wilkinson, a bearded and muscled man wearing jail-issued clothes, steps out while handcuffed. A Maryland state trooper approaches and unlocks the handcuffs. Earl stands free, his expression showing signs of hunger.

name: Shane Falco Emerges from the Tarp and Dresses in the Rain
description: Shane Falco pushes aside a blue plastic tarp and climbs out from inside a worn cabin cruiser moored at the end of a slip. The boat is covered in bird droppings, with a makeshift plywood structure bolted to its roof. Rain falls lightly over the marina. Shane, bare-chested and unshaven, looks up at the gray sky. He pulls on the top half of an old, patched wet suit, zips it up, and shivers as the cold air touches his skin.

name: Lindell Destroys Autograph After Child Receives It from Striking Player
description: A little boy approaches a Redskins player during a protest at the stadium entrance and asks for an autograph. The player signs his program, and the boy begins to walk away. Jerome Lindell, who is picketing with the players, runs after the boy, grabs the program, and tears out the signed page. He throws the pieces on the ground and tells the boy not to ask real players for autographs while planning to watch the replacement team. He then turns to the player and says that giving autographs sends the wrong message to children. The boy leaves quickly.

name: Annabelle Helps Shane After the Bar
description: Shane returns from the bar visibly drunk and collapses into a chair. Annabelle pulls the bed down and remarks that the people from downstairs were looking for drunk Redskins. Shane, embarrassed, admits they found one. She tells him not to feel bad, calling it a rookie mistake. He quickly passes out. Annabelle looks at him without judgment, then unbuckles his belt and begins pulling his pants off.

name: Wilkinson Knocks Out the Judge in Man Maker Drill
description: The Judge, now without his jacket, crouches into a three-point stance across from Wilkinson, who mirrors his position. Teammates form two parallel lines along the sides, watching closely. A voice calls 'hut!' and Wilkinson lunges forward, driving hard into the Judge. The impact sends the Judge flipping backward, landing flat on his back with a heavy thud. He lies motionless, unconscious. Wilkinson steps past him, turns, and slaps hands with Andre and Jamal, a wide grin on his face.

Wilkinson celebrates tackle with teammates

name: Injury on the Field and a Call from the Redskins
description: During a high school football practice, Coach Roland Lamont, wearing a knee brace, demonstrates a drill and shouts, "Cut right on me, now. Right on me!" A player takes the pitch, runs toward him, and steps directly on Lamont's foot with his cleats before cutting around him. Lamont screams, collapses to the ground, and writhes in pain. After a moment, a voice calls out from a distance: "Coach Lamont! Phone call! Long distance. Washington, D.C. It's the Washington Redskins!" Lamont clutches his foot, then manages a smile, looking up toward the sky and saying, "Thank you, Lord!"

name: Wilkinson's Diving Interception Sparks Broadcast Mystery
description: The Patriots' quarterback dropped back and launched a pass toward his intended receiver. Earl Wilkinson, covering the route, darted in front of the receiver and made a diving catch, securing the interception. On the broadcast, Summerall called the play, noting it was Smith's second interception of the game. Beside him, Madden flipped through his notes, then paused. "According to the Redskins, Ray Smith..." he began, reading aloud, "no college listed, no high school listed. Just says he's been a resident of Maryland for the last four years and five months. Likes to embroider."

name: Shane Falco Practices Plays Under Observation
description: The stadium is empty and quiet. A football spirals through the air toward the camera, flying cleanly through a rubber ring attached to the goalpost crossbar. From a reverse angle, the ball is seen passing through the ring. On the field, Shane Falco stands in shorts and a sweatshirt, taking snaps from center Reese Evans. Evans straightens up and says, 'Nice. Try a roll to the right.' He bends over to set another ball. Shane lines up in the shotgun formation, preparing for the next play. A voice from off-screen, Coach O'Neil, mutters, 'Shane 'Footsteps' Falco? This is what you're going to build an offense around?'

name: Madden and Summerall Break Down the Redskins' Final Moments
description: Pat Summerall stands beside John Madden in the broadcast booth, both in shirtsleeves, as the Redskins prepare for their final drive. Summerall remarks that the Dolphins have controlled the Redskins' running game throughout the day. Madden leans forward, drawing on a screen to illustrate the defensive alignment—pointing to the guards, the corners, and the middle linebacker, showing how each level of the defense closes off running lanes. On the field, the Redskins face third and twenty-two with only eight seconds left and trail by a touchdown. Summerall notes the clock and the score, then says the play could be the last of the game. Madden agrees, adding it could be the last play of the season if the players leave the field after this down.

Shane flinches and jumps at the noise. In the stands, a small group of fans dressed in burgundy and gold cheer wildly, raising their drinks as the announcer's voice booms over the loudspeaker: 'Ladies and gentlemen, your Washington Redskins!'

name: Announcer Introduces Team as Fans Cheer
description: The announcer's voice booms over the loudspeaker, introducing the starting lineup of the Washington Redskins. On the field, players emerge one by one, met with a sudden burst of noise from the stands. A small group of fans—Todd, Rod, and Bob—wave their arms and shout, their faces flushed, beer cups in hand. They cheer wildly, clapping and stomping despite the empty seats around them. The sound echoes across the half-filled stadium as the team takes position.

description: At the rear of the stadium, a crowd of Washington Redskins players paces in a circle, some wrapped in fur coats or leather jackets, others holding cell phones to their ears. Their cars—BMWs, Porsches, Mercedes—are scattered nearby. Jerome Lindell, president of the Players' Association, stands with a reporter, speaking into a camera. He declares his support for the players and calls the team owners modern-day robber barons. He accuses them of violating American principles by hiring replacement workers. As he speaks, the picketers grow louder, pointing toward a bus approaching the ramp.

description: A bus slowly approaches the ramp at the rear of the stadium, drawing the attention of the picketing players. The players, dressed in fur coats, leather jackets, and leather pants, begin shouting and pointing toward the vehicle as it draws nearer. Their cars—BMWs, Porsches, Mercedes—are parked haphazardly nearby. Jerome Lindell, president of the Players' Association, stands with a reporter, then turns toward the bus as the commotion grows. The picketers' voices rise in unison, their focus fixed on the approaching vehicle carrying replacement players.

Picketers react to approaching bus with shouting and pointing

name: Interview with Wilson Jones at the Locker
description: A reporter approaches Wilson Jones at his locker while he is dressing. Jones wears a large diamond earring and pauses as the interview begins. The reporter points out that Jones is already one of the highest-paid players and questions why he supports the strike. Jones spreads his arms wide, emphasizing his large frame. He says there are days when he is so injured he cannot dress himself, and he asked management for help, like a valet, but they refused. He responds with anger, saying, 'So, fuck 'em!' A voice from across the locker room calls for quiet as a television is turned up. The screen shows Jerome Lindell, a well-dressed former player, announcing at a press conference that the owners have rejected the players' demands regarding the salary cap. He calls for all NFL players to walk out until the demands are met, urging them to do so with pride and unity. The locker room falls silent. After the announcement, players resume dressing, moving slowly. Wilson Jones says, 'Shit, I'm goin' to Vegas,' and the scene ends.

Wilson Jones explains his need for dressing assistance
Wilson Jones expresses frustration toward management

name: Wilson Jones Reacts to Union Strike Announcement
description: A player calls for quiet as the TV in the locker room is turned up. On screen, Jerome Lindell, the president of the National Football League Players' Association, steps to a podium in a tailored suit. He announces that negotiations with team owners have failed and recommends that all NFL players go on strike, refusing to play until their demands regarding the salary cap are met. He speaks of walking out with pride and solidarity. The broadcast ends. The locker room sits in silence for a moment. Then, players slowly resume dressing, moving with less energy than before. Wilson Jones, the large defensive end with a diamond earring, finishes getting dressed and says, 'Shit, I'm goin' to Vegas.'

name: Nurse Responds to Patient After Redskins Game
description: The room is dark, the blinds closed against the sunlight, with only the blue glow of the television lighting the space. Edward O'Neil, an old man in bed and connected to an oxygen tank, lets out a loud, piercing wail. The door bangs open and Nurse Augustine Ripley, dressed in white, rushes in carrying two syringes. He looks at the TV, which shows the end of a Redskins game with the sound off. 'Did they win or lose?!' he asks. When O'Neil continues wailing, the nurse sets one syringe down, jabs the other into the man's arm, and murmurs, 'Nice medicine for a loss. Keeps us calm. Makes us not so sad. Keeps us on an even keel. Gives us some perspective, doesn't it? And we'll save the winning medicine for next Sunday, won't we?' After the injection, O'Neil says, 'If you keep talking to me like I'm a five-year-old, I'm going to hurt you.' Augustine picks up the phone, hits a speed dial, and hands it to O'Neil. 'We'll want to talk to coach now, won't we?' O'Neil takes the phone and says, 'What the fuck was that?!'
related_events: Old man emits loud piercing wail in dimly lit room
Nurse Augustine Ripley rushes into the room with syringes

description: Madden and Summerall stand in the broadcast booth, speaking to the camera as the Redskins' entrance setup unfolds behind them. A large, inflatable Washington Redskins helmet bobs on the ground near the field exit, flanked by Annabelle and twenty cheerleaders waiting in formation. On air, Madden notes that New England Patriots owner Victor Kiam bought an entire semi-pro team following the player strike. Summerall shifts focus to the Redskins, who have assembled a roster of mostly unfamiliar players. He mentions quarterback Shane Falco, a former Ohio State standout who never succeeded in the pros. Madden recalls the Sugar Bowl where Falco played, and Summerall adds that Falco set a record for interceptions in that game. They acknowledge that for players like Falco, this game represents another chance.

description: A loaf of bread tumbles through the air and lands on the counter in front of a ten-year-old kid after Clifford fails to catch it. The kid smirks and says, 'Nice hands.' Clifford, unamused, asks what else the kid wants. The kid lists a pack of Marlboro Reds, a pint of Martel Cognac, and a box of Trojans, extra long. description: The Manager calls out from the back of the store, holding a portable phone, and tells Clifford that someone is on the phone offering him a chance to play football. Clifford immediately declines, saying he has to work Saturday and is committed to watching the Redskins on Sunday. The Manager speaks into the phone again, then announces that the offer includes payment. When he reveals the amount—ten thousand five hundred dollars—Clifford asks who is calling. A beam of sunlight cuts through the murky water, illuminating a broken bronze football trophy half-buried in the mud. He releases his grip on the hose, drifts downward, and lands softly on the bottom. Kneeling, he picks up the trophy, turning it over in his hands. The football-shaped bronze rests familiarly in his grip as he traces the seams with his fingers.

His body twists as he evades an unseen linebacker, stepping up in the pocket. He rolls left, scanning the murk, then suddenly hurls the trophy forward in a tight spiral. The bronze ball spins into the dim water and out of sight. Shane freezes, arms raised high in triumph, suspended above the muddy seafloor, surrounded by floating debris and dappled light.

name: Prince Leaves Stage with Bodyguards Andre and Jamal
description: The artist formerly known as Prince steps off the stage and grabs a towel from an assistant. He begins walking through the backstage area with bodyguard Jamal leading the way and Andre following behind. As they move, a cell phone rings. name: McGinty Meets With Coaches to Plan Team Roster
description: McGinty sat behind an empty desk as his offensive coordinator, Leo Pilachowski, and defensive coordinator, Christopher Banes, presented the initial team setup. Pilachowski outlined six phone lines with internet access on two of them—one for offense, one for defense. Banes suggested postponing special teams planning, but Pilachowski interrupted to stress the need for a kicker, especially if they lost the coin toss, prompting nervous laughter from both coaches. McGinty remained silent. Pilachowski then proposed rehiring some players cut during the previous season. McGinty scoffed, pointing at the list and saying most had been cut for being terrible. He pulled out his own list, gathered from informal scouting since his retirement, featuring players with unusual backgrounds, many of whom had never played in the pros. He declared they would build a new team from these players—not just to win, but to create a team that would be fun to watch. As he finished, Reese Evans appeared in the doorway, still in his clean Redskins uniform. He said they wouldn’t need a center. McGinty greeted him. Evans admitted he was bored and ready to retire but wanted one last meaningful play. He said he didn’t care about the strike, that he was rich and held no grudge against Mr. O’Neil. All he wanted was one more chance to play, saying he’d rather go out with a broken leg than sit idle. McGinty nodded to Pilachowski, who wrote Evans’ name in the center circle. McGinty welcomed Evans to the new Washington Redskins and told the coaches to find him teammates.

description: Coach Tildon sits in his office, speaking on the phone with O'Neil. Outside, players can be heard showering and dressing, music playing in the background. Tildon tells O'Neil he thinks the player slipped. O'Neil shouts back that it was no slip—he could have scored, that anyone could have scored, even himself despite his age and condition. Tildon responds that the players are going to go out, it’s inevitable, and nobody should get hurt on the last play before a strike that might last the whole season. Enraged, O'Neil calls Tildon a wimp and fires him, yelling for him to get out. He slams the phone down. Augustine picks up the receiver and adjusts O'Neil’s oxygen, turning the flow up. O'Neil takes deep breaths. Augustine asks if he feels better, saying it always helps after firing someone. O'Neil demands that Augustine get Jimmy McGinty, insisting he be brought there that night. He inhales sharply from the oxygen tube as the scene ends.

name: Players Dress and Shower After Practice

name: Lou Takes Bets on a Busy Street
description: Lou Pacifico stands against the wall of a liquor store on a busy side street near Queens Boulevard, taking bets from passersby. A man approaches and says, "Deuce and an eightball on Go Down, Rita in the eighth." Lou quickly jots it down on a small pad. A moment later, another passerby leans in close and whispers something to him. Lou writes again without hesitation, then glances up as activity continues around him.

name: Lou's Mother Shouts About the Washington Foreskins
description: From her window in the four-story walk-up, Lou's mother calls out that he has a phone call. She announces it's from the 'Washington Foreskins.' Lou, standing across the street, shouts back in disbelief, asking if she's out of her mind. She insists, yelling louder that it's the Washington Foreskins—repeating 'Foreskins!' multiple times. People on the street stop and look up, startled by the old woman screaming the strange name. The commotion draws attention as her voice carries down the block.

Mother repeatedly yells 'Foreskins' into the street

name: Lou Kicks Ball, Hits Mafioso
description: A soccer ball rolls toward Lou as he stands on the sidewalk. Without hesitation, he kicks it. The ball arcs down the street, crossing Queens Boulevard. At that moment, an elderly man in a porkpie hat is stepping out of a limo, supported by several men. The ball strikes him in the back of the head, knocking off his hat and dropping him to the ground. The men around him immediately draw pistols and form a circle around the fallen man. Lou sees what happened and ducks into his apartment building. One of the men spots him before he disappears inside.

Soccer ball strikes elderly mafioso on the head
Mafia lieutenants draw weapons to protect fallen leader

Mafia lieutenant spots Lou before he enters building

name: Annabelle Approaches Shane at the Water Cart
description: Annabelle Farrell walks up to Shane while he is drinking from the portable water cart. She introduces herself as the head of the Redskinettes, the cheerleaders. She tells Shane she has been watching him, complimenting his strength, quick release, and ability to read defenses. She mentions seeing his second concussion during the game against Cleveland, recalling the impact vividly, and notes that he still completed the pass. She offers her help, emphasizing that he can come to her for anything. When Shane confirms he understands, she asks if he’s staying at the Hilton, and he says yes. She repeats her offer before walking away across the field.

Annabelle Farrell compliments Shane's performance and resilience

She compliments his strength, quick release, and ability to read defenses. She mentions seeing his second concussion during the game against Cleveland, recalling the impact and noting that he still completed the pass. She tells him he’s doing great and offers her help, saying, 'If there’s anything you need, let me know. And I mean anything.' name: McGinty Tells Clifford to Treat the Ball Like a Girl
description: Coach McGinty stands on the field with Clifford, holding a football. He tells Clifford that all his speed is wasted if he doesn’t catch the ball, reminding him he said the same thing back in high school. Clifford agrees he knows it’s important. McGinty asks if Clifford has ever touched a woman in a romantic way. Clifford says yes, he has. McGinty shoves the football into Clifford’s hands and tells him to touch the ball from now on just like he touches his girlfriends. He says he shouldn’t see Clifford without the ball. As McGinty turns to walk away, Clifford calls him back and asks if he can still touch his girlfriends without letting go of the ball. McGinty pauses, then says yes, if Clifford can manage it.

McGinty instructs Clifford to treat the football like a romantic partner
McGinty hands the football to Clifford with emphasis

name: Clifford Asks About Holding the Ball and Touching Girlfriends
description: After McGinty tells Clifford to treat the football like he treats his girlfriends, always keeping hold of it, Clifford asks if he can still touch his girlfriends without letting go of the ball. McGinty pauses, thinks for a moment, then says yes, as long as he doesn't release the ball.
related_events: Clifford asks if he can still touch his girlfriends without releasing the ball
McGinty approves Clifford's idea of touching girlfriends while holding the ball

name: McGinty Advises and Encourages Shane During Recovery
description: McGinty walks into the room and crouches beside Shane, who is lying on the floor with ice bags on his head, shoulder, elbow, and both knees. In a quiet voice, McGinty tells Shane to look for Murray over the middle, calling him a big, tough kid with good hands. He urges Shane to trust him. Then, McGinty tells Shane there’s still a whole half left, calling him a thoroughbred running against a bunch of nags, saying he can pick the opponents apart. Shane, wincing through the pain, smiles and says, 'You're good. You're really good.'

Mickey Lee chews ice quietly. Cochran sits apart, reading his Bible. McGinty approaches Shane, crouches down, and speaks to him in a low voice.

description: O'Neil sits bundled in a large coat, hunched on the fifty-yard line twenty rows up, an oxygen tank at his side held by Augustine. He watches the field and scoffs as the first player he sees is Footsteps Falco. 'Christ, Jimmy, I ask you to build me a team based on balls and the first player I see is Footsteps Falco?!' McGinty replies that Falco has as much natural talent as any quarterback in the league. O'Neil mocks his footwork, calling them the happiest feet he's ever seen. McGinty insists Falco only needs a boost of self-confidence and declares him the team's quarterback, stating firmly that this is how it will be.

McGinty defends Falco's natural talent as a quarterback

name: O'Neil Seeks Help for the Safety Position
description: O'Neil sits bundled in a large coat, breathing from an oxygen tank held by Augustine. He turns to McGinty, expressing frustration over the team’s lack of a safety with two-a-day practices starting the next day and a game in five days. McGinty defends his choice of quarterback, but O'Neil cuts him off, insisting the defensive position is a crisis. He reveals he has called a friend—the Governor of Maryland—hinting at a connection that might provide a solution. Augustine adjusts the oxygen valve, giving O'Neil a stronger flow, and O'Neil takes deep breaths as the conversation pauses. On the field, Shane throws a perfect spiral through a target circle.

O'Neil reveals he contacted the Governor of Maryland for help

description: Shane, dressed in pads and football pants, opens the door and walks into the locker room. description: Shane walks into the locker room dressed in pads and football pants, then opens the door to the restroom. He begins the awkward process of unfastening his gear to urinate, wrestling with his pants and protective cup. At the urinal next to him, Walter Cochran stands urinating while holding his Bible open behind the flush handle, reading as he goes. Walter greets Shane with a 'Praise the Lord,' and introduces himself as the offensive tackle. After a brief exchange, Walter asks Shane to witness with him, then reaches out his hand. Without looking away from the page, Walter says, 'Praise the Lord, Shane.' Shane responds with a quiet, 'Yeah. Sure.' Walter introduces himself: 'Walt Cochran. Offensive tackle.' Shane nods. name: Bateman's Collision with the Helmet and the Cheerleaders
description: Daniel Bateman sprints out of the tunnel and into an inflated helmet structure. As he runs inside, his foot catches on a wire stretched across the ground. He stumbles and falls hard, bouncing off the elastic inner surface to the opposite side of the helmet. The impact sends him rebounding back and forth before he is launched out of the front of the structure like a projectile. He flies into a group of cheerleaders, knocking down six of them. One girl is thrown so forcefully she loses her shoe. Girls scatter and cry out in pain. Annabelle rushes to the fallen cheerleaders, moving from one to the next. Bateman stands to the side, dazed, as trainers arrive on the field.

Annabelle runs from one fallen girl to the next, kneeling beside them to assess their injuries. Medical trainers rush onto the field with equipment, moving quickly to provide aid. The first biker walks over to the door, listens for a moment, and hears nothing. He starts to turn away when suddenly the door explodes inward.

name: Bateman Storms Meth Lab and Attacks Bikers
description: Daniel Bateman crashes through the door, slamming into the biker who was listening at the entrance. He charges forward, knocking the man down and kicking him in the head. Bateman lunges at two other bikers, head-butting one and forcing the other’s head into the vat of meth mixture. He yanks the man out and strikes him three times in the head with a police blackjack—Rap! Rap! Rap!—sending him collapsing to the ground. Bateman advances toward a fourth biker cowering in the corner just as three windbreaker-clad cops burst in, catching their breath. One stares at the scene. A beeper sounds. The bikers check theirs—neither has it. Bateman pulls his beeper free, frowns at the display, and asks, 'What area code is 703?' The first cop replies, 'Washington, D.C.'

Before he can reach the man, the door swings open and three cops in police windbreakers rush in, breathing hard. They stop and look around at the scene—unconscious bikers on the ground, the meth vat spilled, Bateman standing in the middle. One of the cops exclaims, 'Jesus, Bateman! Why don't you ever wait for us?!'

description: Mickey Lee watches as Roland Lamont begins to unbuckle his heavy knee brace. Mickey asks how it’s possible that Roland only played in one game. You're not a drop back passer. You're a scrambler. Like you were in college. So, we're gonna roll out. A lot. Get used to setting up on the run. You'll live a lot longer.'
